newsitem.title: USA: NHL-RED WINGS' KONSTANTINOV EMERGES FROM COMA.
newsitem.headline: NHL-RED WINGS' KONSTANTINOV EMERGES FROM COMA.

text.p: Detroit Red Wings defenceman Vladimir Konstantinov has emerged from a coma, doctors said Wednesday, but he is still not fully conscious and faces months of rehabilitative therapy.

Konstantinov and team masseur Sergei Mnatsakanov suffered severe head injuries when the limousine they were riding in crashed into a tree on June 13 in the Detroit suburb of Birmingham on their way home from a team golf outing.
Dr. Karol Zakalik said at a news conference at William Beaumont Hospital that Konstantinov appears to be aware of his friends and family members, but is not communicative.
"He's become much more aware of his environment. He's more alert, but he's not fully conscious," Zakalik said.

Doctors said Mnatsakanov, who emerged from a coma two weeks ago, continues to improve and is able to communicate with others. Both men have improved to the point where they will be transferred out of intensive care to a rehabilitation unit in the near future.
The two men face months of daily physical and occupational therapy. Doctors cautioned it is too soon to predict whether they will make full recoveries.
"It's going to be a long rehabilitation process for both of them," Zakalik said. "It really is too early to tell about full recovery."

A third member of the team, Slava Fetisov, suffered chest contusions and a bruised lung during the accident and was released from the hospital last month. The accident occurred six days after the Red Wings won their first Stanley Cup championship in 42 years.

Last week, police revealed that Richard Gnida, the limo driver, had marijuana in his blood before the accident in which the vehicle suddenly veered across several lanes of traffic and hit a tree in the median.

Police are conducting further tests before filing any charges. Gnida could face a felony charge of driving under the influence of narcotics. Regardless of the toxicology tests, police have said they plan to charge Gnida with driving with a suspended license.
